problem: Internal architecture of 'compliance_audit' (type: Store — A persistent data store that holds state across requests and process lifetimes). Node: Append-only, hash-chained tamper-evident store of credentialed-action audit records. Every entry hash-chains to its predecessor so any in-place mutation is detectable; entries are residency-tagged on the same residency-policy framework as other tenant-keyed surfaces; retention policy is declared and bounded by jurisdiction-specific compliance windows propagated through region_coordinator's residency_publisher. The substrate is isolated from operational write planes — usage_meter, metrics_store, gateway, fanout, address_index, chain_router, and tenant_store each write directly to compliance_audit via authenticated append-only RPC, never through a shared operational data path that an operational compromise could alter retroactively. region_coordinator's compliance_audit_owner subsystem owns the audit schema and is the only authority that can publish a new entry-type version. AUDIT MATERIAL IS TWO-TIER: TIER 1 (per-tenant audit-encryption key, shredded on tenant erasure) holds the full audit entry payload including tenant-identifying fields, request payload digests, signing-credential identities, and any other tenant-attributable detail; the hash chain covers Tier-1 ciphertext + entry skeleton; tenant erasure destroys the per-tenant audit-encryption key (crypto-shred), rendering Tier-1 historical entries unreadable while leaving the chain intact and tamper-evidence preserved. TIER 2 (organizational long-lived key under the OOB-anchor key hierarchy, NOT shredded) holds a structural witness — event type, event HLC, originating component, and a hash commitment to the Tier-1 payload — with NO tenant-identifying material; Tier 2 is not subject to erasure. The certificate-of-deletion vouches for Tier-2 witnesses by verifiable hash chain so post-shred a regulator can inspect structure-and-presence of every attested event, verify the hash chain is intact, and verify each Tier-2 hash commitment matches the (now-shredded) Tier-1 payload contents. INBOUND ADMISSION CHECK FOR PER-TENANT WRITES: a write's writer-encrypted-at-HLC must be <= the writer's drain-ack-HLC for the same tenant; a write whose encrypted-at-HLC exceeds the writer's drain-ack-HLC is a protocol violation (ack-after-write contract broken) and is rejected at admission rather than silently shred by a missing key; the rejection is itself logged in compliance_audit's protocol-violation log. The shred mechanism applies only to entries that landed BEFORE the writer's drain-ack-HLC; their decryption is impossible after key destruction by design. CERTIFICATE-OF-DELETION ENTRY: a typed entry assembled by tenant_store and linked here, comprising (per-store erasure attestations + drain-ack receipts + audit-key DESTROYED log entry); each component carries provenance — which writer, which lease/policy_version, which broadcast HLC; certificates are typed as full-ack, partial-with-witnesses, or erasure-incomplete and the type is machine-distinguishable from full-ack. Per-tenant audit-encryption-key lifecycle (issuance, rotation, destruction-on-erasure) is a tenant_store zoom concern; the at-root contract is the two-tier scheme + the late-write rejection rule + the certificate-of-deletion typing. Required entry types include: operator-override admission (chain_router pool_membership_manager, tip_quorum, drain_coordinator, lifecycle_gate force-complete), OOB-anchor use & cert re-rooting, anchor rotation, residency policy_version activation / abort / prepared-orphan, roster mutation (issue, rotate, revoke, retroactive compromise-revocation), offboarding attestation (per-component, including preservation-blocked terminal states), drain-fence broadcast-emit, drain-ack receipts and ack-by-handoff records, certificate-of-deletion (typed full-ack / partial-with-witnesses / erasure-incomplete), protocol-violation log entries, and per-tenant compliance events (lawful-access fetch, erasure tombstone). Connections: region_coordinator --writes_to-> compliance_audit; chain_router --writes_to-> compliance_audit; gateway --writes_to-> compliance_audit; fanout --writes_to-> compliance_audit; usage_meter --writes_to-> compliance_audit; address_index --writes_to-> compliance_audit; tenant_store --writes_to-> compliance_audit. Parent requirements: r-s5-composite-cert-assembly: compliance_audit's certificate of deletion is a verifiable composite of (per-store erasure attestations + drain-ack receipts + audit-key DESTROYED log entry). The assembly contract lives at root: tenant_store collects the per-store attestations and drain-ack receipts under its erasure tombstone for tenant T; lifecycle_gate emits the audit-key DESTROYED event after tenant_store confirms the assembly is closed; compliance_audit links these into a single typed certificate-of-deletion entry whose hash chain covers all three components. Each component carries provenance — which writer, which lease/policy_version, which broadcast HLC. Certificates are typed as full-ack, partial-with-witnesses, or erasure-incomplete.; r-s5-compliance-audit-late-write-rejection: compliance_audit's inbound admission for per-tenant audit writes checks the writer's encrypted-at-HLC against the writer's drain-ack-HLC for the same tenant: a write whose encrypted-at-HLC exceeds the writer's drain-ack-HLC is a protocol violation (ack-after-write contract broken) and is rejected at admission rather than silently shred by missing key; the rejection is itself logged in compliance_audit's protocol-violation log. The shred mechanism applies only to entries that landed BEFORE the writer's drain-ack-HLC; their decryption is impossible after key destruction by design, but their hash-chain inclusion is preserved.; r-s5-audit-tier-witness: Audit material is two-tier. TIER 1 (per-tenant audit-encryption key, shredded on tenant erasure): full audit entry payload including tenant-identifying fields, request payload digests, signing-credential identities, and any other tenant-attributable detail. TIER 2 (organizational long-lived key, NOT shredded): a structural witness of each attested event consisting of event type, event HLC, originating component, and a hash commitment to the (eventually-shredded) Tier-1 payload; Tier 2 contains NO tenant-identifying material and is not subject to erasure. The certificate-of-deletion vouches for Tier-2 witnesses; post-shred, a regulator can inspect the structure-and-presence of every attested event and verify the hash chain. The organizational long-lived key is part of the OOB-anchor key hierarchy under region_coordinator. The per-tenant audit-encryption-key lifecycle remains a tenant_store zoom concern.

versions.note: Naive compliance_audit internal architecture: 7 subsystems (admission_gate, tier_splitter, chain_writer, cert_assembler, retention_enforcer + SubStores chain_log, drain_ack_index, schema_registry), all 4 inherited reqs satisfied at zoom level. CRITICAL K̄=1.25 P̄=0.69; chain_writer K=4 hotspot (single point of append, expected). Ready for stress.

v1 — compliance_audit zoom Session 1 against v0. 10 stressors all BREAKING, 10 derived reqs all satisfied + 4 inherited reqs preserved. ADMISSION_GATE: tenant-state flag {UNFENCED, FENCED} for cold-miss; causal late-write check on (H_w, S_w) vs sealing (H_a, S_a) regardless of arrival order; retroactive-protocol-violation entries on drain-ack arrival; two-phase PROPOSE/ACTIVATE schema activation with deterministic cutover on H_w; HLC-pinned residency-decision-tuple embedded at admission and honored at chain_writer; periodic drain-ack-index-snapshot entries enabling complete restart rebuild; per-(writer,tenant) violation coalescing into bounded violation-summary entries; append-class stamping. TIER_SPLITTER: encrypt-RPC carries (H_w, S_w); typed key-destroyed-encrypt-failure entry on key-destroyed-at-fence response (no silent drop); HLC-anchored audit-key handle lookup; Tier-2 carries routing identifiers (writer_id, tenant_id, sealing tuple) in cleartext for routing-identifier entry types; signs Tier-2 under FORWARD-SECURE per-epoch key. CHAIN_WRITER: per-residency bounded-concurrency micro-batch model (Merkle-root inside, prev-hash links batches); per-class fair-queueing with guaranteed minimum slot shares; commits into pinned partition R_e regardless of current residency policy_version. CHAIN_LOG: micro-batch records; forward-secure Tier-2 epoch model with tier2-epoch-witness and tier2-key-compromise entries; cert-input-pin retention interlock; non-shreddable drain-ack-index-snapshot until superseded; shred preserves entry-hash + Tier-2 + structural integrity. DRAIN_ACK_INDEX: per-(writer,tenant) (H_a, S_a) + violation-coalescing state; per-tenant {UNFENCED, FENCED} flag with irreversible flip; snapshot-restorable. CERT_ASSEMBLER: cert-input-pin opens assembly; per-input verification-mode {Tier-1-and-Tier-2-verified, Tier-2-only-verified, suspect-witness}; full-ack iff structural-presence; partial-with-witnesses iff structural absence or any key-destroyed-encrypt-failure; erasure-incomplete iff DESTROYED missing or preservation-blocked. RETENTION_ENFORCER: pin interlock; non-shreddable most-recent snapshot; retention-shred entries audit-logged in retention-shred lane. SCHEMA_REGISTRY: two-phase PROPOSE/ACTIVATE; (V, V+1, H_act) exposure; deny-by-default for behind replicas. NKP K̄=1.25 P̄=0.69 modularity=0.30 CRITICAL preserved. Hotspots: chain_writer K=4 (single point of append, expected and now load-isolated by per-class fair lanes), chain_log K=3 (audit hub, expected). Incidence K_hyper=0.375 with 51 findings (large because all 10 stressors touched the centerline subsystems; expected for a tightly-coupled audit substrate).

stressors.description: A new (writer, tenant) pair appears at admission_gate with NO prior drain-ack-receipt entry — first ever audit write from that writer for that tenant. drain_ack_index lookup misses. The naive architecture says nothing about whether admission should accept (no fence yet) or reject (no anchor). Operational consequence: every legitimate first write becomes either silently admitted (loses the late-write check until first drain-ack lands) or silently rejected (writer cannot bootstrap). Operators discover the failure mode the first time a brand-new tenant onboards.
stressors.attractor: Implicit admit-if-missing semantics emerge by accident: admission_gate code path defaults to passing-through any (writer, tenant) without an index entry, and the late-write check becomes "best-effort" rather than enforced. Drain-ack-late writes from never-seen pairs slip past undetected; the protocol-violation log under-reports.
stressors.solution: Define the index miss semantics explicitly: a (writer, tenant) pair with no prior drain-ack-receipt entry is treated as having drain-ack-HLC = +infinity (i.e. no fence yet — all writes admitted) UNTIL the (writer, tenant) is bound to a tenant lifecycle (i.e. tenant_store has issued a tenant_cluster identity AND lifecycle_gate has issued at least one drain-fence-broadcast for that tenant), at which point the absence of a drain-ack-receipt becomes drain-ack-HLC = -infinity (no admission permitted). admission_gate consults a tenant-state-flag in drain_ack_index recording whether the pair has entered the fenced regime; tenant_store and lifecycle_gate emit typed entries that admission_gate uses to flip the flag.

stressors.description: A writer issues a per-tenant audit write at HLC=H_w then issues its drain-ack-receipt at HLC=H_a > H_w through lifecycle_gate. Both transit independent network paths to compliance_audit. Under unfavorable scheduling the drain-ack-receipt arrives at admission_gate FIRST; admission_gate updates drain_ack_index to H_a; the late audit write (encrypted-at H_w < H_a) then arrives and is admitted as on-time, even though by the writer-side ack-after-write contract the writer was supposed to flush all in-flight writes before emitting the ack. The result: writes that violated the writer-side contract are silently admitted because compliance_audit has no way to distinguish "arrived late at me" from "emitted late at writer".
stressors.attractor: compliance_audit becomes a "best-effort" late-write detector: only writes that physically arrived after the drain-ack arrived are caught; writes that the writer emitted after its own ack but that traveled faster slip through. The protocol-violation log under-reports the very class of violations the late-write rule was designed to catch.
stressors.solution: Bind the late-write check to writer-side causal ordering, not arrival-time at compliance_audit. Each per-tenant audit write must carry a writer-emitted monotonic per-(writer, tenant) sequence number AND its causally-consistent encrypted-at-HLC. The drain-ack-receipt itself attests "drain-ack-HLC = H_a covers all sequences up to S_a inclusive". admission_gate enforces: a write with sequence S_w admitted at HLC H_w against a drain-ack with (H_a, S_a) is a protocol violation iff S_w > S_a (regardless of arrival order). On admission_gate seeing a write with S_w > S_a where the (writer, tenant) drain_ack_index already contains a sealing drain-ack, the write is rejected as a protocol violation; otherwise the write is admitted and the index is later refined when the drain-ack lands. To detect the inverse case (drain-ack arrives first), admission_gate also retroactively flags any write WITH sequence > S_a that was admitted in the prior bounded retroactive-window, by writing a retroactive-protocol-violation entry into chain_log when the drain-ack lands.

stressors.description: compliance_audit runs admission_gate as multiple replicas (per residency, per region) for throughput and availability. region_coordinator publishes a new entry-type schema version V+1 by appending a schema-version-activation entry into chain_log; admission_gate replicas observe the entry through chain_log replay and update their schema_registry. Replica A applies V+1 at HLC H+ε while Replica B is still on V at HLC H+5ε due to replay lag. During the lag window: a writer submits a new-shape entry to A (admitted under V+1) and an old-shape retry of the same logical event to B (admitted under V). Two entries with different schemas land in chain_log for the same logical event; downstream consumers and cert_assembler cannot deterministically distinguish the canonical record.
stressors.attractor: Schema activation becomes "eventually consistent across replicas" with no upper bound on skew window; logical events double-write under different schemas during the window; cert_assembler downstream develops ad-hoc reconciliation logic to pick one of the two; the schema_version field becomes advisory rather than authoritative.
stressors.solution: Schema activation is two-phase across admission_gate replicas with a quorum-witnessed activation HLC. Phase 1 (PROPOSE): region_coordinator compliance_audit_owner appends a schema-version-PROPOSE entry into chain_log with proposed activation HLC H_act in the future; admission_gate replicas observe the propose entry and pre-load V+1 alongside V into schema_registry. Phase 2 (ACTIVATE): replicas refuse to admit any entry under V+1 BEFORE H_act and refuse to admit any entry under V AT OR AFTER H_act. Replicas that have not observed the PROPOSE entry by H_act minus a bounded readiness window must refuse all admissions for the affected entry types (deny-by-default) until they catch up. The schema_registry now exposes (V, V+1, H_act) and admission_gate uses the writer-encrypted-at-HLC against H_act to pick the schema deterministically — no replica skew can cause cross-schema double-write of the same logical event.

stressors.description: A legitimate per-tenant audit write (encrypted-at-HLC H_w within the writer drain-ack-HLC bound) is in-flight at tier_splitter, awaiting the tenant_store encrypt-RPC. Concurrently lifecycle_gate emits the audit-key DESTROYED event for the same tenant; tenant_store destroys the per-tenant audit-encryption key. Three sub-cases: (a) encrypt-RPC arrives at tenant_store BEFORE DESTROY — encrypts and returns ciphertext; chain_writer appends; certificate-of-deletion later assembled INCLUDES this entry’s Tier-1 ciphertext but the key is gone — Tier-1 is unreadable from the moment cert is assembled, which is consistent with crypto-shred semantics. (b) encrypt-RPC arrives AFTER DESTROY — encrypt-RPC returns key-destroyed; tier_splitter has a payload it cannot encrypt and the entry is causally legitimate (S_w ≤ S_a). (c) encrypt-RPC and DESTROY interleave atomically — partial state. The naive arch does not specify what tier_splitter does in (b) — drop the entry (loses an attestation), append as Tier-2-only (loses tenant-attributable detail at the time it would have mattered most), or fall through to admission_gate as a violation (misclassifies a legitimate-by-causality write).
stressors.attractor: tier_splitter develops ad-hoc fallback logic: silent drop, or quietly downgrade to Tier-2-only without flagging, masking the fact that a tenant-attributable event happened that no one can ever read. Operators only discover the gap when a regulator asks why structural witnesses for a tenant outnumber recoverable Tier-1 payloads in a window where Tier-1 was supposed to exist.
stressors.solution: Make the encrypt-RPC contract two-tier-aware and the failure path explicit. tier_splitter requests encryption against the per-tenant key with the writer-encrypted-at-HLC H_w and writer-sequence S_w as part of the request. tenant_store rejects encrypt-RPCs whose H_w is at or after the audit-key destruction-fence-HLC H_destroy with a typed key-destroyed-at-fence response carrying H_destroy. On that response, tier_splitter writes a typed key-destroyed-encrypt-failure entry into chain_log via chain_writer carrying ONLY the Tier-2 structural witness (event type, H_w, originating component, AND the routing/key-destroyed reason), with NO Tier-1 ciphertext. The cert_assembler later treats the presence of any key-destroyed-encrypt-failure entries for a tenant as an erasure-incomplete signal (the writer believed it had a legitimate write to make AFTER the destroy fence — its drain-ack contract was therefore violated upstream); the certificate-of-deletion type degrades to partial-with-witnesses or erasure-incomplete accordingly. tier_splitter NEVER drops silently; the failure mode always lands as a typed entry.

stressors.description: A region-wide bulk-offboarding wave triggers from lifecycle_gate: thousands of tenants drain-fence concurrently. Per-tenant audit writes from 7 parent-scope writers funnel into chain_writer, plus drain-ack-receipts, plus retention_enforcer scheduled crypto-shred entries, plus operator-override admissions, plus cert_assembler appends for tenants reaching erasure. All entries within a single residency partition serialize through chain_writer CAS-on-tip-hash. Under sustained contention CAS retries dominate, latency-sensitive entries (cert_assembler trying to close out tenants past the regulatory window) starve behind bulk-shred and bulk-attestation traffic. Operators resort to manually pausing retention or extending erasure deadlines, undermining the audit guarantees.
stressors.attractor: chain_writer becomes a global serialization bottleneck per residency; operators apply ad-hoc back-pressure that bypasses or delays the very audit entries the system needs most under wave conditions; certs land late or in degraded type because their inputs could not all reach chain_log within the regulatory window.
stressors.solution: chain_writer admits a bounded-concurrency append model with per-residency append-class lanes. The chain remains strictly hash-linear within a residency partition, but chain_writer batches admitted entries into bounded micro-batches (each micro-batch is a single CAS-on-tip-hash committing a sequence of N entries with internal Merkle-tree-of-entries roots; the chain prev-hash links micro-batch to micro-batch and a sub-proof inside the batch links each entry’s entry-hash). Append classes (cert_assembler, drain-ack-receipt, protocol-violation, normal per-tenant write, retention-shred, schema-activation, operator-override) each hold a guaranteed minimum share of micro-batch slots so cert_assembler and protocol-violation cannot starve behind bulk-shred or bulk per-tenant traffic. Per-class fair-queueing parameters are owned by region_coordinator (configuration entry types in chain_log) so operators tune them via the same audit substrate they constrain.

stressors.description: A long-tail tenant erasure for a tenant whose drain-fence broadcast and per-store erasure attestations occurred years ago (e.g. preservation hold expired late, or assembly trigger delayed). cert_assembler walks the assembly inputs to verify chain presence — the per-store erasure attestation entries from years past; the drain-ack receipts from years past. retention_enforcer has, in the meantime, retention-shredded those entries (Tier-1 ciphertext gone) per the active retention policy for that residency / entry-type. cert_assembler can verify Tier-2 structural witness presence (event type + HLC + originating component + hash commitment) but cannot recover the Tier-1 detail (which writer attested precisely what). The naive arch does not specify whether the resulting certificate is full-ack (Tier-2 still proves the components attested) or erasure-incomplete (Tier-1 unrecoverable so provenance detail is lost).
stressors.attractor: cert_assembler implements an ad-hoc rule (e.g. "Tier-2 witness is enough" OR "any shredded input downgrades the cert") inconsistently across components, leading to a population of certificates whose typing is not comparable across cohorts and whose interpretation drifts as retention policies change.
stressors.solution: Two complementary mechanisms. (1) Retention-policy interlock: retention_enforcer must NEVER shred any chain_log entry that is a named assembly input for an open or pending certificate-of-deletion. tenant_store, on opening an assembly trigger for tenant T, registers a cert-input-pin (typed entry into chain_log) listing the entry-hashes the cert will reference; retention_enforcer reads chain_log and treats pinned entry-hashes as retention-extended until the certificate-of-deletion entry referencing them is itself appended (or the pin is explicitly released by tenant_store). (2) Define cert typing semantics for legitimate post-shred reads: cert_assembler classifies an input as Tier-2-only-verified vs Tier-1-and-Tier-2-verified based on whether the input is still readable at Tier-1 at assembly time; the certificate-of-deletion record carries a per-input verification-mode field. A cert with all inputs Tier-2-only-verified retains full-ack typing iff all expected inputs are present in chain_log (structural-presence is what regulators ultimately need post-shred); cert_assembler degrades to partial-with-witnesses ONLY when an expected input is structurally absent.

stressors.description: The organizational long-lived signing key for Tier-2 witnesses is compromised at HLC=H_c. Until rotation completes (rooted in the OOB-anchor key hierarchy at parent scope), an attacker can mint forged Tier-2 witnesses indistinguishable from legitimate ones. Worse: pre-existing Tier-2 witnesses signed under that key are now "questionable" — a verifier years later cannot tell whether a given Tier-2 was signed before H_c (legitimate) or after (potentially forged) without a separate, externally-anchored signing-history record. Even after key rotation, decades-old certificates referenced by current cert-of-deletion records inherit doubt. Compliance-audit verifiability across decades — the whole point of the OOB-anchor-rooted Tier-2 — is broken.
stressors.attractor: Compliance-audit verifiability becomes "verifiable until the next compromise" rather than the multi-decade guarantee assumed by certificate-of-deletion semantics. Every key compromise event invalidates retroactive trust in earlier Tier-2 witnesses; cert_assembler has no recourse but to mark all certificates from before the rotation as "doubtful" or suppress the issue entirely.
stressors.solution: Tier-2 signing uses a forward-secure / append-only key-evolution scheme rooted in the OOB-anchor hierarchy: the active Tier-2 signing key advances one epoch per chain_log micro-batch (or per fixed bounded chain-prefix), and the public verification material for each epoch is itself committed into chain_log under the OOB-anchor key on epoch transition (typed tier2-epoch-witness entry). A compromised epoch-K key cannot mint signatures attributable to epoch K-1 or earlier (forward security); a verifier years later validates a Tier-2 witness against the epoch verification material committed in the epoch-witness entry, which is itself anchored in the prev-hash chain. Compromise rotation appends a typed tier2-key-compromise entry naming the compromised epoch and the new active epoch; cert_assembler treats any Tier-2 witness from a compromised epoch as Tier-2-suspect (degrading verification-mode to suspect-witness) without invalidating prior epochs. The epoch-witness chain itself is verified against OOB-anchor signatures, and OOB-anchor compromise is bounded by region_coordinator parent-scope OOB-anchor M-of-N quorum.

stressors.description: A per-tenant audit write enters admission_gate at residency policy_version V; admission_gate resolves the tenant residency to partition R under V and forwards the entry through tier_splitter to chain_writer. While the entry is queued at chain_writer awaiting its micro-batch slot, residency policy_version flips to V+1 (parent-scope 2PC commit lands a new policy that relocates the tenant to partition R prime). chain_writer at append time observes V+1 active. Without explicit pinning, two outcomes are possible: append into R (the resolved partition at admission time, but per V+1 the entry is in the wrong residency = tenant-attributable data crossing residency boundary) or append into R prime (rerouted, but Tier-1 ciphertext was constructed under the audit-key handle bound to V). Either way the entry violates an invariant.
stressors.attractor: compliance_audit silently writes some entries into the wrong residency partition during the V→V+1 cutover window; downstream residency audits flag the substrate itself as the violator; operators cannot retroactively prove which partition was correct at the entry HLC.
stressors.solution: Pin the residency policy_version to the writer-encrypted-at-HLC, not the chain-writer-commit HLC. admission_gate stamps every admitted entry with a residency-decision-tuple (residency_version V_e, partition R_e) computed from the writer-encrypted-at-HLC under the residency policy active at that HLC; the tuple is part of the entry record passed through tier_splitter to chain_writer. chain_writer commits the entry into partition R_e regardless of the residency policy_version active at commit time. The residency policy_version 2PC at parent scope is HLC-anchored on the policy effective HLC H_pv, so for any writer-encrypted-at-HLC H_w the active policy_version is deterministic. If a write arrives at admission_gate with H_w in the future relative to admission_gate observed residency policy_version (admission_gate has not yet seen the activation), admission_gate denies-by-default per the existing parent-scope sticky-deny pattern. tier_splitter constructs Tier-1 ciphertext under the per-tenant audit-key handle that was active at H_w (tenant_store key-handle lookup is HLC-anchored).

stressors.description: admission_gate process restart loses the in-memory drain_ack_index. Per the naive arch the index rebuilds by replaying chain_log forward from a checkpoint to recover (writer, tenant) -> (drain-ack-HLC, sealing-sequence). But retention_enforcer has retention-shredded some old drain-ack-receipt entries (Tier-1 ciphertext gone) and the rebuild walker either cannot recover the (writer, tenant) attribution from Tier-2 alone (if Tier-2 omits the writer-tenant binding for tenant-attributable entries) OR can recover but uses a stale checkpoint that pre-dates the most recent drain-ack. The rebuilt index has a partial baseline; admission_gate resumes serving with a baseline that admits writes that should have been rejected, AND admits unfenced writes for tenants whose FENCED state-flag is not yet recovered.
stressors.attractor: admission_gate restart silently downgrades enforcement strength: late-write protection becomes available only for tenant pairs that have had drain-ack activity within the recent retention window; older fenced-tenant-pairs revert to UNFENCED-by-default and the protocol-violation log under-reports without operator visibility.
stressors.solution: Two complementary mechanisms. (1) Tier-2 structural witness for drain-ack-receipt and tenant-fence-state-transition entries MUST carry the (writer_id, tenant_id, drain-ack-HLC, sealing-sequence) tuple in cleartext (these fields are non-tenant-attributable structurally — writer_id and tenant_id are routing identifiers also stored in numerous non-shreddable parent-scope locations like tenant_store erasure tombstones, so including them in Tier-2 does not violate the no-tenant-identifying-material rule for crypto-shred, since shred destroys *content* not the *fact-that-tenant-T-existed*). This guarantees rebuild from chain_log Tier-2 alone is complete even after retention-shred of Tier-1. (2) admission_gate persists periodic drain_ack_index snapshots as typed snapshot entries into chain_log itself (small, bounded by N tenants * M writers); on restart it rebuilds from the most recent snapshot plus forward replay; snapshots are themselves retention-pinned by retention_enforcer (snapshot entries are non-shreddable until superseded by a fresher snapshot). The combination guarantees admission_gate can never resume with a stale baseline.

stressors.description: A compromised parent-scope writer (or a buggy one) emits a sustained stream of late writes against many tenants simultaneously. admission_gate dutifully rejects each as a protocol-violation, but per the inherited late-write-rejection contract every rejection is itself logged as a typed protocol-violation entry into chain_log. The flood becomes an amplification attack: each rejected write costs one Tier-2 entry of chain_log space; chain_writer micro-batch capacity fills with violation entries; legitimate cert_assembler and drain-ack writes starve in their fair-queue lanes (per s5) but the violation lane itself overflows; storage growth on chain_log accelerates beyond retention budget; downstream replicas fall behind on Tier-2 epoch transitions.
stressors.attractor: compliance_audit becomes a self-DOS substrate: the very contract that ensures violations are auditable becomes a vector to fill the audit log with attacker-chosen content; operators face the choice of breaking the rejection-is-itself-logged invariant (silently dropping violations and losing audit trail) or accepting unbounded chain growth.
stressors.solution: Coalesce repeated protocol-violations from the same (writer, tenant) pair into a single bounded-state violation-summary entry. admission_gate maintains a per-(writer, tenant) violation-counter in drain_ack_index that increments on each rejected late write within a sliding window of width W. The FIRST violation in a window emits a typed protocol-violation entry into chain_log carrying the rejected-write metadata (encrypted-at-HLC, sequence S_w, sealing (H_a, S_a)). Subsequent violations within W increment the counter without emitting further entries. On window close (or counter saturation, or another distinct-cause violation arrives), admission_gate emits a single typed violation-summary entry carrying (count, first-seen-HLC, last-seen-HLC, min-S_w, max-S_w). chain growth from a flood becomes O(distinct-(writer,tenant)) per window, not O(write-rate). The summary entry is sufficient for an external operator/regulator to detect the flood, identify the writer, and trigger upstream credential revocation; per-write detail is not preserved (acceptable: the writer is misbehaving by definition, full per-write fidelity is an upstream concern).
